rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG / FY2016 COLLECTION OF TAXES / RECEIVABLES SUMMARY / JUNE 30, 2016`, PDF page 48 of the FY2016 annual town report -- the MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE section, twenty levy years 1997 to 2016, and the heading `OTHER EXCISE TAXES` under which nothing is printed. THE PAGE IS PRINTED CLIPPED, AND THAT IS WHY IT CANNOT BE FOOTED. Page 47 of the same report prints this same schedule for property taxes with EIGHT columns -- FORWARD, COMMITTMENTS, ADJUSTMENTS, REFUNDS, PAYMENTS, ABATEMENTS, TRANSFER, BALANCES -- and every one of its rows closes on `forward + committments + adjustments + refunds + payments + abatements + transfer = balances`, the negatives printed in parentheses. Page 48 stops after PAYMENTS: ABATEMENTS, TRANSFER and BALANCES are not printed, here or anywhere else in the report. Read off the rendered page, the ruled table simply ends at the right-hand edge of PAYMENTS. So there is no closing figure for the motor vehicle excise receivable, the identity page 47 states cannot be run, and the balance sheet does not supply it either -- page 20 prints one combined `EXCISES $243,852.65` against this page's five columns netting $303,306.05, which are not the same quantity and cannot be differenced. WHAT IS ASSERTED HERE IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE DIGITS, AND IT IS WEAKER THAN ARITHMETIC: the twenty levy years run 1997 to 2016 without going backwards, which catches a row dropped, duplicated or mis-ordered and cannot see a misread digit. COVERAGE: the page prints 48 money tokens and all 48 are recorded below; no figure on the page is left out and none is invented. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: what the town's motor vehicle excise receivable was at 30 June 2016. That figure is not published. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the Collector's own receivables control, or an un-clipped printing of this worksheet -- the same document that would close page 49.

rows.proof: `LUNENBURG CULTURAL COUNCIL / Fiscal Year 2016 / LCC Account Form`, submitted 13 October 2015 and completed 10 January 2016, PDF page 57 of the FY2016 annual town report. It is the Massachusetts Cultural Council's own account form, reproduced in the report. THE PAGE WAS NOT IN THE TRACKER: eighteen money figures, below the fifteen-figure threshold's reach because they are printed in prose lines rather than in a ruled table, so the page was ABSENT from the annual-report page universe rather than unfinished. TWO IDENTITIES CLOSE, BOTH TO THE CENT, and both are the form's own: state revenue $1,100.00 plus municipal revenues $13.98 plus other revenues $0.00 is the printed Total Revenues $1,113.98; and the account balance at 30 June 2015 of $6,902.40 less $4,213.00 spent to 1 November 2015 less $925.00 of pending encumbrances is the printed Available Remaining Balance $1,764.40. A THIRD CLOSES AND IS NOT DECLARED: $8,979.42 brought forward plus $1,113.98 of revenue less $3,191.00 of expenditure is the $6,902.40 end balance, computed at read time. verify_page_reads.py's identity grammar takes `a,b,c=d` (all added) or `a-b-c=d` (all subtracted after the first) and this one is MIXED, so it is recorded here rather than asserted. AND THE $6,902.40 IS PRINTED TWICE IN THIS REPORT: page 35's SPECIAL REVENUE FUNDS schedule gives the `Arts Lottery Fund` a FORWARD 7/1/2015 balance of $6,902.40, the same figure this form gives as the council's balance at 30 June 2015. That agreement is between two documents the town published and is offered as corroboration; it is not the check that proves this page. NOT ASSERTED: the form's last two figures, `Amount Available for Granting in FY2016: $6,464` and `Total granted in FY'2016: $6,464`, are printed in WHOLE DOLLARS where everything above them carries cents. $1,764.40 available plus the $4,700 FY2016 allocation is $6,464.40, so the printed $6,464 is the rounded figure and not the sum of the printed parts. Both are recorded as printed and neither is corrected.

rows.proof: `CAPITAL PLANNING` / `Fiscal Year 2017 Capital Plan`, PDF page 94 of the FY2016 annual town report. CIP Tracker | Priority | Item | Amount | Cumulative Cost -- twelve items, ranked 1 to 12. THE PAGE WAS NOT IN THE TRACKER AT ALL. A page enters the annual-report page tracker on fifteen recognised money figures and this one prints twenty-five, but it sits in the narrative section of the report rather than the Town Accountant's schedules, so nothing had looked at it. It is a real capital table with its own printed total. WHAT CLOSES: the twelve item amounts add to the `Total` the page itself prints under them, $780,975, to the DOLLAR. These are whole-dollar figures with no cents anywhere, so the tie is exact and no tolerance is declared. AND THE CUMULATIVE COLUMN IS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT CHECK, computed at read time: each item's Cumulative Cost is the previous item's cumulative plus this item's amount, and that holds for all twelve rows, ending at $780,975 -- the same figure as the printed Total. It is published here as `line` rather than asserted because it is a running sum rather than a column that adds, and the verifier has no grammar for a figure that depends on the row above. WHAT THE PAGE SAYS ABOUT THE $619,475: the prose beside the table states that only items 1-10 were included in the Town Manager's FY2017 Recommendation, and item 10's printed cumulative is $619,475 -- which is the figure the same paragraph gives for the FY2017 capital budget, funded by cash with no borrowing. That agreement is the document's, not ours, and it is recorded rather than asserted.

rows.proof: THE FY 2017 OMNIBUS BUDGET as voted at the Annual Town Meeting of 5 May 2016, Article 15, pages 144-149 of the FY2016 annual town report. LINE # | ACCOUNT | FY 17, 91 line items in thirteen sections. THE SECTION IS SIX PAGES, 144 TO 149, and TWO OF THEM ARE HOLES IN THE PAGE MAP: page 144 carries the heading row and the whole Maturing Debt & Interest section, and page 149 carries Schools, Library and the `Total Omnibus` -- the two pages a table cannot be proved without, and neither was listed. WHAT CLOSES. The thirteen section totals sum to the printed `Total Omnibus $33,802,328.00` EXACTLY. Twelve of the thirteen foot their own line items exactly: Maturing Debt, General Govt., Central Purchasing, Protection, Health & Sanitation, DPW, Facilities & Buildings, Solid Waste/Recycle, Assistance, Schools, Public Library -- and the four `Subtotal` rows inside Protection and Assistance are nested, not additional. THE ONE THAT DOES NOT IS THE TOWN'S, AND IT IS THE $45. `Total Gen Govt.` is printed $2,615,696.00 on page 145. Its own fourteen line items -- 4 Liability Insurance $219,061.00, 5 Workers Compensation $64,984.00, 6 Group Health Insurance $1,907,185.00 (page 144); 7 Group Life Insurance $22,635.00, 8 Physicals $3,500.00, 9 Print Town Reports $12,000.00, 10 MRPC Assess $3,278.00, 11 Historical Commission $3,000.00, 12 Band Concerts $4,200.00, 13 Reserve Fund $50,000.00, 13A Salary Reserve Fund $93,996.00, 14 Unemployment Expense $10,000.00, 14A Unemployment Exp.-Stab Fund $-, 15 Medicare Town's Share $221,902.00 (page 145) -- sum to $2,615,741.00. THE PRINTED SUBTOTAL IS $45.00 LOW. AND THE OMNIBUS'S +$45 IS THE SAME $45. `Total Omnibus` is built from the section totals and ties to them to the cent, so the under-printed `Total Gen Govt.` propagates: the 91 line items sum to $33,802,373.00 against a printed $33,802,328.00, out by exactly $45.00, and it is the ONLY break anywhere in the six pages. An extractor that made this close would be wrong. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: which of the fourteen line items, or the subtotal itself, carries the error. Every figure here is read off a born-digital text layer, so none of the fifteen is a misread, and the document does not say which it intended.

rows.read_by: claude-opus-5 reading the PAGE'S OWN EMBEDDED BITMAP. pdfplumber reports 208 words of text on PDF page 150 -- all of them the warrant article prose above and below the table, NONE of them inside it -- and one DeviceRGB image 721x577 at ~85 dpi carrying the whole grid, so the TABLE is a photograph even though the page is not (rule: apply the text-layer test to the REGION the figures are in). The bitmap was taken straight out of the PDF stream; it is a raw FlateDecode DeviceRGB sample array with NO container, so `get_data()` cannot be handed to PIL and `Image.frombytes('RGB',(721,577),...)` was used with the stream's own /Width, /Height and /ColorSpace, then composited over white through its /SMask. Read at 2.8x whole and again at 6x in two four-step bands, each band carrying the Grade column pasted beside it. NO RECOGNITION WAS USED.
rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2017`, 20 grades against STEP 1 to STEP 8, 160 HOURLY rates. THE COLUMN NAMES ARE THE PRINTED HEADER, READ AND WRITTEN DOWN: `Grade | Step 1 | Step 2 | Step 3 | Step 4 | Step 5 | Step 6 | Step 7 | Step 8`. THIS PAGE PRINTS NO TOTAL ANYWHERE and there is no arithmetic on it to close, so the check is COVERAGE, declared and asserted on every run: 20 grade rows, numbered 1 to 20 without going backwards, each carrying exactly the 8 rates its printed header promises. That proves the SHAPE and not the digits, and it is weaker than arithmetic for exactly that reason. THE SECOND INSTRUMENT IS THE DOCUMENT'S OWN SECOND PRINTING. The FY2016 annual town report prints this schedule TWICE, as two DIFFERENT bitmaps: page 150 inside the warrant of the Annual Town Meeting of 5 May 2016 (721x577, sha256 60d202c1...) and page 186 inside the warrant of the Special Town Meeting of 28 November 2016 (727x582, sha256 a8fb30ef...). Both were transcribed from their own bitmap and the two readings AGREE IN 160 OF 160 CELLS, 0 disagreements -- and that is also a finding about the document: the November special town meeting reprinted the May schedule UNCHANGED. BE CLEAR WHAT THAT IS AND IS NOT. It is two printings read by one reader, and the second read was not blind to the first, so it is not double-entry; what it does rule out is a defect in either stored bitmap, since two independently stored images cannot be wrong the same way. A REGULARITY, TESTED AND REPORTED, NEVER USED AS THE PROOF: the steps sit about 3% apart and it is tempting to use that as the arithmetic this page lacks. IT DOES NOT HOLD TO THE CENT. round(step_1 x 1.03^(n-1)) reproduces 95 of the 140 non-STEP-1 cells and MISSES 45; compounding step to step with rounding at each step misses 45. Every miss is a single cent, which is what makes the rule tempting and what makes it useless as a check -- an error in the cents place would survive it untouched. Nothing on the page states 3%, and the ABSENCE of the regularity is the finding. ONE TYPOGRAPHIC FEATURE, READ AND RECORDED RATHER THAN NORMALISED: the GRADE 1 row prints its eight rates with NO dollar sign -- `9.44 9.72 10.01 10.31 10.62 10.93 11.26 11.61` -- while every other row prints `$`. It is the same on both pages. The figures are stored as read; the missing sign is the document's.
